extras.name: Omaha
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid and the Missouri carry the fit; the 1868 E. Ruger sheet is the steepest (near-vertical) whole-city view in the pool (the 1905 Austen 'panoramic' oblique is the recorded dupe): drawn from a high vantage across the Missouri River - the river a foreground strip with steamboats and a railroad along the sheet's bottom, a thin hill-horizon band across the top - the city grid fills the sheet beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Indianapolis
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid and the White River carry the fit; the 1925 E. G. Spink Company sheet is the steepest (near-vertical) - in fact the ONLY - whole-city view in the pool: drawn from a high vantage to the south (the White River side) - the river a band along the sheet's bottom, Union Station and the Hotel Spink lower-centre, the grid running up to the State Fair Grounds at the top (north) - no horizon band - the city grid fills the sheet beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Columbus
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid and the Scioto River carry the fit; the 1872 H. H. & O. H. Bailey sheet is the ONLY drawn whole-city view in the pool (the LOC .jpg/.tif scans are its same-sheet dupes, the DPLA reproduction the smaller same-sheet dupe): a true OBLIQUE drawn from a high vantage to the south (the Scioto River side) - the river's bend a foreground band lower-left, the Statehouse square at centre, the street grid receding north toward a visible sky/horizon band along the sheet's top (open farmland beyond the built-up area) - unlike the Omaha/Indianapolis near-verticals - the built-up grid still fills the sheet beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Memphis
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid and the Mississippi carry the fit; the 1870 A. Ruger sheet is the steepest (true oblique) whole-city view in the pool (the 1887 Wellge and the 1887 'Appeal' newspaper page are the only other drawn whole-city views - both shallower and worse-scanned): drawn from a high vantage across the Mississippi River (from the Missouri side) - the river and its steamboat landings a foreground band lower-left, the city up the bluffs across the centre (the downtown grid, the squares, the rail yards), the open plain to the horizon upper-left, a visible sky band with clouds along the sheet's top - unlike the Omaha/Indianapolis near-verticals, like the Columbus 1872 true oblique - the built-up grid still fills the sheet beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Portland
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid and the Willamette carry the fit; the 1890 J. McI. Wood perspective sheet is the steepest (near-vertical) - in fact the ONLY - drawn whole-city view of the pool that passes the 4000-px width gate (the 1880 J.K. Gill sheet's only scan is 1742 px, the two NYPL 1880s scans 3072 px): drawn from a high vantage to the NORTHWEST (the Eastside bluffs) looking southeast - the Willamette River runs diagonally upper-left to lower-right with the downtown grid on both banks, a long steel-truss railway bridge mid-sheet, river traffic, Mt. St. Helens and the Cascade range a background mountain band at right, a sky band along the top, prominent-building vignettes framing the sheet - the grid fills the sheet beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)
